scenario: A volunteer is preparing a welcome for people attending a drop-in craft session.
memory_focus: People may leave whenever they need to, without explaining why.
detours: Discuss greeting arrivals naturally, then how to explain a simple activity.

scenario: A volunteer helps sort donated art supplies for a free community workshop.
memory_focus: Opened supplies can be offered if usable; they need not be new.
detours: Discuss keeping different materials separate, then inviting participants to share supplies.

scenario: A volunteer helps a community centre prepare for a board-game afternoon.
memory_focus: The user has offered to explain game rules but not to supervise children.
detours: Discuss choosing an approachable first game, then helping someone join mid-session.

scenario: A volunteer helps collect stories for a community scrapbook.
memory_focus: Contributors can choose whether their names appear alongside their stories.
detours: Discuss making space for short contributions, then asking before changing someone's words.

scenario: The user is trying to work out why a friend missed their usual phone call.
memory_focus: The friend had warned that their phone would be unavailable while its battery was being replaced.
detours: Discuss how the user spent the evening; then discuss a television programme they both enjoy. Finally ask what the friend had said about their phone.

scenario: A volunteer coordinates a small group folding programmes for a local performance.
memory_focus: The user wants to take part in folding rather than supervise the others.
detours: Discuss making the task comfortable, then how to keep the group chatting naturally.

scenario: A volunteer prepares an informal welcome for a neighbourhood repair café.
memory_focus: The user will greet visitors; repair decisions remain with the people examining the items.
detours: Discuss making waiting time pleasant, then how to introduce a visitor to a helper.

scenario: A volunteer works with others to organise donated jigsaw puzzles.
memory_focus: A puzzle with an uncertain piece count must be labelled as unverified.
detours: Discuss grouping boxes by size, then how to make browsing easy for visitors.

scenario: A volunteer considers how to support an intergenerational conversation session.
memory_focus: Participants should be free to decline a question.
detours: Discuss choosing open prompts, then making pauses feel comfortable.

scenario: The user tells a story about returning home with the wrong umbrella after lunch.
memory_focus: They realised the umbrella was not theirs because its handle was wooden, while theirs had a rubber grip.
detours: Discuss the sudden rain; then discuss how they contacted the restaurant. Finally ask what first alerted them to the mix-up.

scenario: A person wants to mend a loose fabric loop on a reusable shopping bag.
memory_focus: The user wants to reinforce the existing loop rather than replace the bag.
detours: Discuss practising stitches on scrap cloth, then keeping sewing supplies organised.

scenario: Someone is repairing a loose page in a personal notebook.
memory_focus: They want the page to remain readable on both sides.
detours: Discuss protecting the work surface, then letting a repair dry undisturbed.
